questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Derives the sector area formula from the fraction of a circle.
questions.stem: A sports club groundskeeper needs to explain to a junior colleague why the area of a circular sector is worked out as one half times radius squared times the angle in radians. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: Start with the fraction of the whole circle that the sector occupies. A full circle of radius r has area πr^2 and a central angle of 2π radians, so a sector of central angle θ covers the fraction θ/(2π) of the circle. The area is then πr^2 × θ/(2π) = (1/2)r^2θ. The formula therefore works only when θ is in radians, because the fraction-of-a-circle argument compares the angle with 2π radians, the total in one turn. A degree measure would need the factor π/180 applied first.

questions.explanation: The answer should derive the formula from the fraction of a full circle, noting that a full circle is 2π radians with area πr^2, and conclude area = (1/2)r^2θ. It should state that radians are required.
questions.hint: Compare the sector with the whole circle of 2π radians.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explains how a directed angle records the sense of a turn.
questions.stem: A sports club coach wants to explain how a directed angle records the sense as well as the size of a turn, and why a clockwise turn carries a negative sign. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: A directed angle measures a turn with a sign attached to its sense. Turning anticlockwise is given a positive sign and turning clockwise a negative one, so the same physical turn can be written +45° or -45° depending on the direction of travel. Angles are understood modulo a full turn of 2π radians, so -45° and 315° point to the same direction, but they describe different motions, and the directed angle is the one that records which way the player actually turned.

questions.explanation: The answer should explain that a directed angle carries a sign for its sense, with anticlockwise positive and clockwise negative, and that angles are taken modulo 2π. It should note that coterminal angles can describe different motions.
questions.hint: Clockwise is negative, anticlockwise is positive.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.topic: Special angles on the unit circle
questions.learningObjective: Explains how the exact special angle values come from the unit circle.
questions.stem: A sports club mathematics group wants a written explanation of how the exact trigonometric values at 30°, 45° and 60° are obtained from the unit circle. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: Each special angle gives a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the unit circle radius 1. At 30° the triangle is half an equilateral triangle, so the side opposite 30° is 1/2 and the other leg is √3/2, giving sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 30° = √3/2. At 45° the triangle is isosceles right, so both legs are √2/2, giving sin 45° = cos 45° = √2/2. At 60° the triangle is the complement of the 30° one, so sin 60° = √3/2 and cos 60° = 1/2.

questions.explanation: The answer should explain that each special angle gives a right triangle with hypotenuse 1, and list the 30°, 45° and 60° values with reasons such as the half equilateral triangle and the isosceles right triangle.
questions.hint: Each special angle gives a right triangle with hypotenuse 1.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explains how to find the reference angle of a direction.
questions.stem: A sports club coach needs to explain to a new member how to find the reference angle of a direction given in degrees. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: First decide which quadrant the direction lies in. For 0° to 90° the direction is already its own reference angle, at exactly 90° the reference angle is 90°, for 90° to 180° it is 180° - θ, for 180° to 270° it is θ - 180°, and for 270° to 360° it is 360° - θ. A reference angle is always the acute angle between the terminal side and the nearest horizontal axis, and it is never negative, so the signs of the ratios are then set by the quadrant.

questions.explanation: The answer should give the reference angle for each of the four quadrants and explain that it is the acute angle to the nearest horizontal axis, then note that the quadrant fixes the signs of the ratios.
questions.hint: First find the quadrant, then measure to the nearest axis.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explains how quadrant signs follow from the reference angle.
questions.stem: A sports club analyst wants a written explanation of how the signs of sine, cosine and tangent follow from the quadrant once the reference angle is known. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: The reference angle gives the size of each ratio, and the quadrant gives its sign. In the first quadrant all three ratios are positive, in the second only sine and tangent are positive while cosine is negative, in the third sine and tangent are negative while cosine is also negative, and in the fourth cosine and tangent are positive while sine is negative. This is seen by reflecting the unit circle: moving a terminal side into the second quadrant reflects the cosine coordinate across the vertical axis, and moving into the third quadrant reflects it across the horizontal axis as well.

questions.explanation: The answer should give the sign pattern in each quadrant and tie it to reflecting the unit circle, explaining that the reference angle fixes the size while the quadrant fixes the sign. It should note that tangent keeps the sign of sine.
questions.hint: Quadrant one all positive, then reflect.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explains the arc length formula and why radians make it simple.
questions.stem: A sports club groundskeeper must explain how the length of an arc relates to its central angle, and why the radian measure makes that relationship a single multiplication. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length equals the radius. If a central angle of θ radians is used, the arc it cuts off is θ times the radius, so the arc length is s = rθ. Because the definition fixes the radian to an arc-length ratio, no extra constant appears, unlike degrees where a conversion factor of π/180 must be applied. The same idea gives the sector area, since the sector is the fraction θ/(2π) of the whole circle.

questions.explanation: The answer should define the radian as an arc-length to radius ratio, derive s = rθ, note that degrees need a conversion factor, and mention that the sector area follows from the fraction of the circle.
questions.hint: A radian is an arc length equal to one radius.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explains the coordinate formula for a rotation about the origin.
questions.stem: A sports club coach needs a written explanation of how a rotation about the origin transforms the coordinates of a point, and why the length of the point's vector is preserved. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: A counterclockwise rotation by θ sends the point (x, y) to (x cos θ - y sin θ, x sin θ + y cos θ), because the new x-coordinate is the projection onto the new horizontal direction and the new y-coordinate is the projection onto the new vertical direction. The length from the origin is unchanged because the rotation matrix has orthogonal columns of unit length, so x^2 + y^2 is preserved. A quarter turn anticlockwise therefore sends (x, y) to (-y, x).

questions.explanation: The answer should give the rotation formula, explain that the new coordinates are projections onto the rotated axes, and show that the length is preserved. It should illustrate with the quarter turn.
questions.hint: New coordinates are projections on the rotated axes.

answer.exemplar: The angle 135° lies in the second quadrant, 45° past the vertical, so the point on the unit circle is (cos 135°, sin 135°). questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Defines the reference angle and explains its uniqueness.
questions.stem: A sports club youth coach needs a written explanation of what a reference angle is and why every angle has exactly one. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: The reference angle of a direction is the acute angle between its terminal side and the nearest of the two horizontal axes, the positive x-axis or the negative x-axis. Every direction has exactly one because the terminal side lies in exactly one of the four quadrants, and each quadrant has a single axis adjacent to it. The reference angle is therefore always between 0° and 90° inclusive, never negative, and it captures the shape of the angle while leaving the sign of each ratio to the quadrant.

questions.explanation: The answer should define the reference angle as the acute angle to the nearest horizontal axis, explain that the quadrant makes it unique, and note that it lies between 0° and 90° and carries no sign.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explains how to use a reference angle and a quadrant for a ratio.
questions.stem: A sports club analyst needs a written explanation of how to use a reference angle and a quadrant to find the exact value of a trigonometric ratio. Write the explanation.

answer.exemplar: First find the reference angle of the direction, which gives the size of the ratio, and then use the quadrant to attach the sign. For example, for 220° the reference angle is 40°, so |cos 220°| = cos 40°, and since 220° is in the third quadrant the cosine is negative, giving cos 220° = -cos 40°. The same method works for sine and for tangent, remembering that tangent has the sign of sine because it is sine divided by cosine.

questions.hint: Reference angle gives size, quadrant gives sign.
